receipts.reason: Fixed-vector unipotence and complete reducibility definitions are coherent; the equivalence and identity-component clauses are supplied by the current bridge, including the hereditary subgroup argument and disconnected finite-component averaging.

Translation spreads the regular point supplied by homogeneous regularity; prime localization gives regularity at all scheme points and the perfect-field dictionary gives smoothness. Pure dimension now uses points lying on unique components, avoiding ambiguity at component intersections.
The orbit-fibre, quotient-topology and invariant-function clauses give the stated categorical factorization by affine charts. The classical closed-point Spec convention and empty case are explicit.

The current connected orbit supplier gives locally closed irreducible orbits and the exact dimension/boundary clauses. Finite component cosets and equal stabilizer dimensions prove the disconnected extension; descending orbit dimensions gives existence of closed orbits. Closed orbit plus finite stabilizer agrees with dimension-zero stabilizer. The current orbit lemma supports the identity-component reduction because connected orbits form disjoint closed components inside a full orbit.

Reviewed the full radical/Levi/central Jordan argument. Exponentials generate a Zariski-dense subgroup, using smooth subgroup dimensions and algebraic connected-group integrality. The unipotent closures use Lie flags and polynomial additive-group characters. Closed subgroups inherit fixed-vector unipotence by the inserted faithful upper-unitriangular/logarithm-curve argument, closing the identity-component converse. Finite averaging, rational semisimplicity, natural Reynolds projection and invariant linearity preserve all clauses. Compact-orbit averaging is conditional on the stated dense compact subgroup; finite-dimensional affine-dependence reduction proves the convex hull compact, so the unique-invariant convex-hull assertion is established.

The positive ideal has finitely many homogeneous positive-degree generators: each component remains inside the ideal by the grading. Degree induction shows these generate the algebra, including an empty list and degree-zero field.

Invariant linearity gives R(IA)=I and injectivity of ideal extension; ascending-chain stabilization gives Noetherian invariants. Naturality gives surjective invariant maps and preservation of stable gradings.

The polynomial algebra is Noetherian by the direct finite-variable supplier; Reynolds ideal theory makes its graded invariants Noetherian and the corrected graded-generation lemma yields finite algebra generation.

Equivariant embedding plus invariant surjection proves finite generation. Reynolds ideal contraction and maximal ideals prove quotient surjectivity and closed generator-independent image. Stable radical ideals give closed images/intersection equality; orbit-dimension descent and separation give the unique closed orbit. The corrected rational-localized Reynolds computation proves (A_f)^G=(A^G)_f with localized injection only, including zero divisors. Fibre constancy and saturated principal charts give full categorical universality; integral closedness gives normal invariants. All six clauses remain.

The action-map fibre at a complex point is a stabilizer translate, with constant component dimension. The affine-local source-point fibre bound yields an open source locus, whose identity-section pullback proves stabilizer upper semicontinuity. Dimension zero gives exactly finite stabilizers; all stated locus consequences follow.

The current affine quotient maps a closed invariant subset to a closed subset; its radical ideal separates a point outside its image by Nullstellensatz, and pullback gives the required invariant with the two prescribed values.

Orbit-boundary dimension excludes positive-dimensional stabilizers from a stable fibre. A separating invariant produces saturated principal charts with all orbits closed and finite stabilizers. Localization identifies the sheaf, unique closed orbits give orbit fibres, and saturation of opens gives quotient topology. The localized injection/rationality caveat is explicit.

Unique monomial expansion and the test t=2 force off-diagonal coefficients to vanish, and substitution z=xy is injective. The incorrect absolute-value expression for negative powers was replaced by the direct strict inequalities.

Verified all four orbit classes, punctured-axis closures, stabilizers, invariant coordinate xy and stable geometric quotient. The explicit equivariant product map (t,c)→(t,c/t) proves the full trivial principal-bundle assertion.
The trivial action on one point is algebraic, its unique orbit is closed, and its stabilizer is the infinite multiplicative group, directly refuting the exact assertion.

The published Noether theorem explicitly assumes a finite group. The hyperbolic multiplicative-group action does not meet that hypothesis; the remark states a hypothesis comparison only and imports no unproved finite-group reduction.

Reviewed the corrected cocycle: at (g,h,x) it maps L_ghx via g inverse and then h inverse to L_x. Character twists are valid total-space algebraic actions; the tautological action linearizes O(-1), and its dual linearizes O(1). No existence theorem is consumed.

The maximal-L-block box bound proves generation of S^(kL) in degree one for k≥max(1,N−1), including S_d=0 and nilpotent generators. Standard graded quotient charts give a closed projective embedding and the twisting-sheaf identification. The corrected standard-Veronese formula and the arbitrary larger-k bound retain all sufficiently large multiples of L.
The exact external result is recorded as unproved, with connectedness and normality hypotheses, a source URL and explicit nonuse. No theorem here infers a supplied linearization from that record.

Tensor-power cocycles, finite affine trivializing covers, finite product-coordinate expansions and separating fibre evaluations prove the rational section action without choice. Nonvanishing identities and equivariant multiplication prove the graded ring assertions. The projective constant-function conclusion now uses the exact current published constant-functions theorem and inherits AC only for that conclusion and its degree-zero consequence.

The scheme clauses now use the associated reduced finite-type complex scheme of X, so affine morphisms, sheaves and scheme surjectivity have a consistent meaning while arbitrary complex-scheme targets are retained. Geometric orbit fibres explicitly mean complex closed-point fibres. The categorical universal property and classical specialization are distinguished precisely.

The section-ring multiplication/rationality supplier supports the definition. Proj and localized degree-zero chart constructions use the correct ring, and positive tensor powers give the exact Veronese. The definition assumes AC and does not assert invariant finite generation.

The ample-power theorem provides a subsystem embedding and projective cohomology gives finite-dimensional H0. Affine-chart surjectivity makes the complete-system map a closed immersion into its coordinate-open locus, and proper source to separated target makes its image globally closed. Equivariant evaluation proves both equivariance and the stronger isomorphism i*O(1)=L^m as G-linearized sheaves.

All good-quotient clauses descend over a target open cover. Disjoint closed point-preimages under an invariant h give constancy on complex fibres. The finite-type kernel pair X×_Y X, closed equalizer, closed-point density and a common field-valued point of each pair of residue fields give constancy on all topological fibres even for arbitrary scheme Y and nonreduced kernel pair. The complement-image clause proves affine target-preimages saturated and their images open; invariant sheaf descent proves categorical factorization with uniqueness of both map and sheaf. The complex-point geometric criterion and quotient topology retain the exact classical specialization.

Invariant sections of positive powers define semistability, and finite stabilizer plus closed orbit in that locus defines stability. Embedded comparisons now explicitly require the isomorphism of G-linearized sheaves, excluding the character-twist defect while preserving the canonical embedding supplied by the lemma.

Reviewed the f-torsion split and invariant complement: an invariant localized fraction has a representative fixed in the torsion-free complement. The Reynolds formula is well defined even with zero divisors and taking degree zero gives the exact chart equality.

For every positive-degree section, a sufficiently high positive power lifts to a homogeneous form by Serre vanishing for the ideal sheaf; its unchanged nonvanishing locus is a closed subspace of an affine standard chart. Invariance gives G-stability, and the semistable cover follows. The embedding identification is explicitly compatible with the linearization.

For each residue degree j mod m, the projective section-module supplier gives a finite tail, and cohomology finiteness gives a finite initial part. The polynomial action factors through the homogeneous coordinate image, making the full section ring finite over that finitely generated algebra. This does not assume surjective restriction in every degree; the empty scheme is included. The actual ample-sheaf dependency is declared.

Finite homogeneous algebra generators lie in a finite-dimensional graded rational generating submodule. Its symmetric algebra surjects equivariantly onto A; the Reynolds invariant-surjection clause and finite-module invariant theorem give finite generation, with homogeneous generators.

The current Proj associated-sheaf and graded localization suppliers identify the chart function ring and its invariants. The added Reynolds module splitting gives a nonzero algebra in every prime fibre, hence scheme surjectivity; applying the same argument to invariant radical quotients gives closed scheme images, and Reynolds applied to I+J=C gives disjoint scheme images. Explicit finite monomial residue splitting proves finite generation of the degree-zero ring; the affine quotient theorem gives all scheme good-quotient clauses and localization gives overlap compatibility. Empty X is now handled directly before assuming degree-zero=C.

Invariant finite generation and projectivity give the target, including the explicit empty-X/zero-ring exception to degree-zero=C. Degree-zero invariant ratios prove each chart is the full preimage of its target chart. Separation removes positive-dimensional stabilizers near a stable point and orbit-boundary dimensions give closed charts. The repaired closed-fibre/saturated-chart argument proves closed-chart finite-stabilizer points stable without asserting scalar values for homogeneous sections. Unique closed affine orbits give the full fibre-closure criterion, and closed-chart geometric quotients give open saturated stable image and the invariant-chart equivalence.

The full section ring is finite over the homogeneous coordinate image, not equated with it. Homogeneous integral relations and Reynolds projection give invariant coordinate-chart coverage; the extension-of-sections supplier identifies both localized degree-zero rings with the same chart functions and hence canonically identifies both Proj quotients. Compatible G-linearized embedding is required explicitly. Invariant surjection lifts coordinate forms to ambient forms; the closed invariant embedded X contains orbit closures, proving the full ambient semistable/stable comparison. Positive powers give Veronese compatibility and all good-quotient clauses remain.

The full section-ring Veronese is no longer equated with the homogeneous coordinate ring. The main theorem supplies canonical localized chart/Proj identifications and the compatible linearized embedding transfers all open/saturated/geometric assertions. Arbitrary invariant section charts are saturated via degree-zero ratios; a closed quotient fibre keeps orbit boundary points inside the chart, proving both directions of the invariant-chart stable criterion. Every positive power and the all-stable geometric case are retained.

On the projective point, the trivial linearization has all constant sections invariant, while the identity-character twist has none in positive degree. The two invariant rings have Proj a point and empty respectively; this directly refutes dependence only on the underlying sheaf.

The monomial weight 2i−n+kn gives all invariant rings and semistable loci for standard, opposite unit twists and higher twists. Standard nonzero-coordinate locus is the single transitive orbit with finite μ2 stabilizer, hence closed there, without a scalar-section level-set assertion. The fixed point lies in the closure of every nonfixed orbit on each unit-twist affine chart, so the stable loci are empty and those quotients are not geometric.
